integrity: The complete 1984 Langford numerical study was inspected through its center-manifold normal form, explicit model equations, axisymmetric torus, parameter values, phase-locking sequence, period doublings, chaotic bands, and thick-torus discussion. Targeted full-document searches found no average, conditional, or moment formulation and no statistical-variance theorem. The 1979 foundational torus-interaction source was checked for the steady/Hopf interaction and doubly periodic torus result. The 2008 same-model source was checked for its day-resolved publication date and torus-bifurcation/control scope. A later same-system mathematical record supplies primary MSC 34A34. The two conditional laws, angular marginal, variance identities, equality classification, and standard-parameter radius were independently reconstructed and replayed with the packaged checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the axisymmetric Langford subfamily and does not include the symmetry-breaking term used to generate later chaotic regimes.
Compact invariant support must stay off the symmetry axis.
The circular-orbit equality classification assumes \(1+\rho\beta\ne0\) and positive \(G(\beta)/(1+\rho\beta)\).
The result determines selected conditional means and variances rather than the complete invariant distribution or torus rotation number.
The original 1984 model source is month-resolved in the checked record; the structured date uses the earliest checked day-resolved same-model publication instead of inventing a 1984 day.
An equivalent short mean-height observation could remain in older unindexed torus-bifurcation literature.
title: Exact mean-height calibration and radial activity in the axisymmetric Langford torus model
